title: 3-Stage Hack Escaped Meta's Muse AI Agent?!
summary: Researchers at NebuSec disclosed a three-stage exploit chain targeting Meta's Muse personal AI agent that chained a bundled Chromium flaw, data exfiltration past the Sentinel egress gate, and a Linux kernel memory-corruption bug to reach root inside the user VM. Meta patched the flaws prior to public disclosure, and the underlying VM boundary and hypervisor remained intact.
raw_text: So check this out—security researchers just mapped out a gnarly three-step exploit chain against Meta's Muse personal AI agent. According to NebuSec, the chain started with a bug in the agent's bundled Chromium renderer for shell execution, moved to exfiltrating chat history and memories past the Sentinel egress check without approval prompts, and used a Linux kernel flaw to hit root inside the user's VM. Here's the wild part: the researchers reported that kernel escape worked over 99.9 percent of the time inside that per-user virtual machine. Thankfully, Meta patched all of these vulnerabilities before going public, and the core VM boundary and hypervisor held firm. Honestly, this is huge for personal AI agents because giving an assistant browser power plus persistent memory creates a really juicy attack surface if sandboxing isn't airtight. title: Rackspace Spot Breach Leaked Kubernetes Secrets!
summary: Rackspace restored its Rackspace Spot managed Kubernetes service on November 21 after shutting down administrative access following a November 17 intrusion. raw_text: So check this out for anyone running cloud clusters—Rackspace just brought its Rackspace Spot managed Kubernetes platform back online on November 21 after a serious security scare.
